name: BetterHelp
summary: Online therapy platform connecting adults with licensed therapists via messaging and live video, focused on convenient access to psychotherapy for common mental health concerns.
description: BetterHelp is a large online therapy platform that matches adults with licensed therapists for ongoing care via secure messaging, live video, audio, and chat sessions. Instead of paying per session, members pay a weekly fee billed every 4 weeks for access to asynchronous messaging plus 1 live session per week (frequency can vary). BetterHelp is designed for people with mild to moderate depression, anxiety, stress, and relationship issues who want convenient access to psychotherapy from home. It is not a crisis service and is not appropriate for people with severe psychiatric symptoms, active suicidality, or complex conditions that require in-person, higher-level care.
patient_summary: BetterHelp is an online therapy service. You fill out a questionnaire, get matched with a licensed therapist, and then work with that therapist through messages and weekly live sessions by video, phone, or chat. It’s designed for adults with depression, anxiety, stress, or relationship issues who want therapy from home and are comfortable using their phone or computer. It does not prescribe medication and is not a good fit if you are in crisis, have severe symptoms (like active suicidal thoughts, psychosis, or severe substance use), or need very intensive, in-person support.

Support for trauma history (when clinically appropriate for outpatient teletherapy)

linked_conditions.context: Individual psychotherapy (including CBT and related approaches) is a first-line treatment for mild to moderate depression. BetterHelp connects users with licensed therapists who may use these approaches via telehealth. The platform is generally appropriate for people with mild to moderate symptoms who are medically stable and not in acute crisis.

CBT and related psychotherapies are strongly supported for generalized anxiety disorder. BetterHelp therapists may provide CBT and other evidence-based approaches via secure video or messaging for adults with mild to moderate GAD symptoms.

Trauma-focused therapies (like TF-CBT, CPT, EMDR) can be delivered via telehealth when clinically appropriate. Some BetterHelp therapists may offer trauma-informed care, but the platform is not a substitute for specialized, higher-intensity care for severe or unstable PTSD.

Psychotherapy can help with coping skills, routines, and relapse prevention for bipolar disorder, but medication management and careful monitoring are essential. BetterHelp does not provide medication or emergency services and is best used as an adjunct for stable adults already followed by a prescriber.

contraindications: Active suicidal ideation with plan or intent (requires emergency and/or intensive in-person care)
Recent suicide attempt or self-harm requiring urgent follow-up
Severe substance use disorder needing detox or structured addiction treatment
Court-ordered or mandated treatment that requires in-person assessment or documentation
People who cannot safely use technology privately (e.g., unsafe home environment, domestic violence where messaging could be monitored)

efficacy_data.comparison_data: Multiple trials and meta-analyses suggest internet-based and video-based psychotherapy can produce symptom reductions comparable to in-person therapy for many adults with depression and anxiety.
efficacy_data.patient_text: Decades of research on online and video-based therapy (not specific to BetterHelp) suggest that, for many adults with depression and anxiety who are medically stable, talking with a licensed therapist by video or secure messaging can help reduce symptoms in ways similar to traditional in-person therapy. BetterHelp follows this general telehealth model but does not yet have large, independent randomized trials of its specific platform.

exclusions: Active suicidal thoughts or recent attempt
Severe substance use needing detox or intensive treatment
Need for in-person, higher level of care (partial hospitalization, IOP, inpatient)

sections.heading: What BetterHelp Does
sections.text: BetterHelp is an online therapy platform that matches adults with licensed therapists for ongoing care via secure messaging and live sessions. After completing an intake questionnaire about your history, symptoms, and preferences, the platform suggests one or more therapists. You can send unlimited messages to your therapist and typically have about one live video, phone, or chat session per week (frequency can vary by plan and provider). BetterHelp focuses on convenience and access: sessions are remote, you do not have to travel to a clinic, and you can switch therapists if the match does not feel right. The service does not prescribe medication, is not a crisis line, and is not a substitute for higher-level in-person care when needed.

sections.heading: How Well Does Online Therapy Work?
sections.comparison: Internet-based and video-based CBT vs. in-person CBT (not BetterHelp-specific)
sections.text: Multiple clinical trials and meta-analyses show that guided internet-based cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) and video-based psychotherapy can be roughly as effective as traditional in-person CBT for many adults with depression and anxiety. These studies are not specific to BetterHelp, but they support the overall model of secure telehealth therapy. BetterHelp’s own internal outcomes data suggest that many active users report symptom improvement over time, but those data come from self-reported surveys without independent peer review or randomized comparison groups.
sections.patient_text: Talking with a licensed therapist online (by video or secure messages) can help many people with depression and anxiety in similar ways to in-person therapy, as long as their symptoms are not so severe that they need hospital-level care. BetterHelp follows this general teletherapy model. However, there are not yet large, independent randomized clinical trials specifically testing the BetterHelp platform.

sections.heading: Who Is BetterHelp Best For?
sections.text: BetterHelp is generally best for adults who:
items: Have mild to moderate depression, anxiety, or stress and are medically stable
Prefer talk therapy and are open to CBT or related approaches
Want flexible scheduling and the ability to message a therapist between live sessions
Feel comfortable using video, chat, and messaging to communicate
Have privacy and a quiet space at home or work to attend telehealth sessions
May have difficulty accessing in-person therapy due to time, transportation, or local provider shortages
not_recommended: People with active suicidal thoughts, recent suicide attempts, or self-harm behaviors needing urgent or intensive care
People with uncontrolled psychosis, mania, or other severe symptoms requiring close in-person monitoring
Individuals with severe substance use disorders who likely need detox or structured addiction treatment
Those who need in-person assessment for disability, legal, court-ordered, or fitness-for-duty evaluations
People who do not have a private, safe place to join sessions

items.description: BetterHelp works with licensed mental health professionals (for example, psychologists, licensed professional counselors, licensed clinical social workers, and marriage and family therapists) who are authorized to practice in the user’s state or country. The exact credentials depend on your location and the professional you are matched with.
items.evidence: Psychotherapy delivered by licensed clinicians has robust evidence for depression, anxiety, and related conditions when appropriately matched to severity.

items.description: You can send secure text, audio, or video messages to your therapist between live sessions. Therapists typically respond within a set time frame (often 24–48 hours on weekdays), though response frequency is not truly 24/7.
items.evidence: Asynchronous messaging can supplement live sessions and increase feeling of support, but it is not a crisis service and response times vary.

items.description: Most plans include around one live session per week via video, audio, or live chat (exact frequency may vary). These sessions function similarly to traditional 45–50 minute therapy visits, but are conducted remotely.
items.evidence: Video-based psychotherapy shows outcomes comparable to in-person therapy for many conditions when delivered by trained clinicians.

items.description: The intake questionnaire is used to suggest a therapist based on your preferences and concerns. If the match does not feel right, you can request a different therapist without starting a new subscription.
items.evidence: A good therapeutic fit is a strong predictor of engagement and outcomes in psychotherapy.

items.description: BetterHelp periodically offers group webinars or psychoeducational workshops on topics like stress management, anxiety, and relationships at no extra cost for subscribers.
items.evidence: Psychoeducation and skills workshops can support individual therapy but are not a substitute for one-to-one care when needed.

sections.heading: Privacy & Data Security
sections.summary: BetterHelp uses encryption and access controls to protect messages and account data, but has faced regulatory scrutiny for past data-sharing with advertising platforms. Grade: C+
items: Account and message data are transmitted over encrypted connections.
Therapists access your information through secure portals with login controls.
BetterHelp states that it no longer shares mental health information with advertising platforms under a 2023 FTC order.
Personal information and app-usage data are still used internally and may be shared with service providers for analytics, infrastructure, and support.
Therapy transcripts are not shared with employers or insurers unless you explicitly authorize it.
data_collected: Ongoing messages and notes related to your therapy.
Technical data such as IP address, device information, and usage patterns.
Payment and billing details processed via third-party providers.
data_shared: Payment data with payment processors (e.g., Stripe, Apple, Google).
Service-level data with infrastructure and analytics providers to run the platform.

Historically, BetterHelp shared certain user and visitor data with advertising platforms such as Facebook and Snapchat, leading to a 2023 FTC order prohibiting sharing of health data for advertising and requiring a $7.8 million settlement and refunds.
concerns: Past sharing of data with advertising platforms raised concerns about trust and confidentiality.
Online therapy platforms, including BetterHelp, may collect more detailed engagement and usage data than a typical in-person clinic.
Not covered by HIPAA in the same way as many traditional health systems; review the current privacy policy carefully before signing up.
sections.hipaa_note: BetterHelp states that it takes privacy and security seriously, but it is not a traditional HIPAA-covered entity like many hospital systems. A 2023 FTC order requires additional safeguards and prohibits sharing health information with advertisers. Users should read the current privacy policy and terms of service before using the platform.

sections.heading: How to Start Using BetterHelp
steps: Go to betterhelp.com or download the BetterHelp app on iOS or Android.
Complete the intake questionnaire about your mental health history, current symptoms, and what you hope to work on.
Create an account and review estimated weekly pricing based on your location and answers.
If cost is a concern, complete the financial aid questionnaire (if available) to see if you qualify for reduced rates.
Review the proposed therapist match and profile. If the match does not feel right, you can request a different therapist.
Once matched, send an introductory message and schedule your first live session (video, phone, or chat).
Discuss goals and preferences with your therapist in the first few sessions, and agree on how often you will meet and how you will use messaging between visits.
tips: Use headphones and a private space during sessions to protect your privacy.
Be as honest as you feel safe being about symptoms and history; accurate information helps your therapist recommend appropriate strategies.
Clarify expectations for message response times and live session frequency with your therapist.
If you feel the fit is not right after a few sessions, consider requesting a different therapist—it is common to try more than one provider.
Do not rely on BetterHelp for emergencies; know your local crisis numbers and nearest emergency department.
common_mistakes: Signing up when in active crisis instead of contacting emergency services or a local crisis line.
Assuming BetterHelp provides medication management or formal diagnoses for legal or disability purposes.
Expecting immediate, dramatic change; psychotherapy often takes several weeks to show clear benefits.
Not raising concerns about therapist fit or style—switching providers is allowed and sometimes necessary.
Sharing very sensitive information in messages without first understanding your privacy comfort level and the platform’s policies.

items.comparison: Another large online therapy platform offering messaging and live sessions with licensed therapists. Pricing and formats are similar. Some users may prefer Talkspace’s interface or provider network; others may prefer BetterHelp.

Local or regional telehealth clinics that offer video visits with psychiatrists and therapists through hospital systems or medical groups. Often able to prescribe medication and coordinate with primary care, but may have longer wait times or more limited schedules.
Traditional, face-to-face therapy in your local area. Less convenient than online, but may be better for complex or severe conditions, crisis-prone patients, or people who prefer in-person rapport.

faqs.a: Yes. BetterHelp connects you with licensed mental health professionals (for example, psychologists, licensed professional counselors, or clinical social workers) who provide psychotherapy via telehealth. The care itself is similar to traditional talk therapy—it’s the format and delivery (online instead of in-person) that are different. As with any therapy, quality can vary based on the individual therapist, your fit with them, and how actively you participate.

faqs.q: Who is a good fit for BetterHelp?
faqs.a: BetterHelp is generally best for adults with mild to moderate depression, anxiety, stress, or relationship issues who are medically stable and not in immediate crisis. It works well for people who prefer remote care, have reliable internet and a private space, and are comfortable using messaging and video. It is not a good fit for people with active suicidal thoughts, recent suicide attempts, uncontrolled psychosis or mania, or severe substance use disorders—those situations usually require more intensive, in-person support.

faqs.q: Does BetterHelp prescribe medication or provide psychiatry?
faqs.a: No. BetterHelp provides psychotherapy only. Its therapists cannot prescribe medication or order lab tests. If you may need antidepressants, mood stabilizers, ADHD medications, or other psychiatric medicines, you will still need to see a prescriber in person or through another telepsychiatry service. Many people use BetterHelp for therapy while working with a separate psychiatrist, primary care physician, or nurse practitioner for medication management.

Pricing changes over time and can vary by location and promotions, but most users pay roughly $60–$90 per week, billed every 4 weeks. This usually includes unlimited messaging with a therapist and about one live session per week (video, phone, or chat), though details can vary. Financial aid may lower the cost for some users. Always check the current pricing on betterhelp.com before signing up.

BetterHelp does not bill insurance directly. Some people may be able to use HSA/FSA funds or request out-of-network reimbursement from their insurance with a receipt or invoice, but this is not guaranteed and depends on your plan. If using insurance is important, it’s worth checking whether local clinics, group practices, or other telehealth services in your network might be a better fit.

BetterHelp uses encryption and access controls to protect messages and account data, and therapists are expected to follow professional confidentiality standards. However, the company has faced criticism and a 2023 FTC order for past sharing of certain data with advertising platforms. Under that order, BetterHelp is now prohibited from sharing health information for advertising and must adopt stronger privacy safeguards. It is important to read the current privacy policy and decide whether you are comfortable with how your information will be used.

For many adults with mild to moderate depression and anxiety who are medically stable, online therapy with a licensed clinician can be a reasonable alternative to in-person therapy. However, in-person care is often better for people with severe symptoms, frequent crises, complex trauma, or conditions requiring close monitoring. Some people also simply prefer in-person connection. In many cases, the choice comes down to symptom severity, safety, personal preference, and what is realistically available in your area.

faqs.q: Is BetterHelp appropriate if I have suicidal thoughts or I’m in crisis?
faqs.a: No. BetterHelp is not a crisis service and should not be used when you are in immediate danger of harming yourself or someone else. If you have active suicidal thoughts with a plan or intent, have recently attempted suicide, or feel unsafe, you should contact your local emergency number, crisis hotline, or emergency department right away. Once you are safe and medically stable, a therapist (online or in person) can help with longer-term treatment planning.

faqs.q: Can I choose my therapist or switch if it’s not a good match?
faqs.a: You cannot usually browse every therapist profile before starting, but the matching process suggests a provider based on your questionnaire responses. If the fit does not feel right after a few sessions, you can request a new therapist at no extra charge. It is common to try more than one therapist before finding a good match, and switching is part of normal care—not a failure.

faqs.q: How quickly will my therapist respond to messages?
faqs.a: BetterHelp therapists generally respond to messages within a set time frame (often within 24–48 hours on weekdays), but they are not online 24/7 and response times can vary. Messaging is meant to supplement scheduled live sessions, not replace emergency or real-time support. If you need immediate help, you should call a crisis line or emergency services instead of waiting for a message reply.

faqs.q: Can BetterHelp help with trauma or PTSD?
faqs.a: Some BetterHelp therapists have training in trauma-informed care and may use approaches like CBT or elements of trauma-focused therapies. For people with mild to moderate, stable PTSD symptoms, telehealth therapy can be helpful. However, for severe, complex, or unstable PTSD—especially when there is dissociation, self-harm, or safety concerns—specialized in-person treatment is usually recommended. If you have a trauma history, it’s important to discuss your symptoms and safety needs openly with a clinician and ask what level of care they recommend.

editorial.reviewStatement: Description, clinical context, and safety guidance for BetterHelp were reviewed against current teletherapy evidence, BetterHelp’s public materials, and 2023 FTC regulatory actions as of December 2025. Because there are no large, independent randomized controlled trials specific to this platform, all clinical claims are framed at the level of general online psychotherapy evidence rather than BetterHelp-specific efficacy.
